status: DESIGN_REGISTERED 2026-09-25; amendment 1 adopted 2026-09-30 (user decision) before any result: the formal run starts as soon as the receipt is regenerated; implementation complete
question: Can per-source calibration of administrator release-time statements keep the information gain of the statement while bringing the recovery risk inside a pre-set budget, and does it then beat, at matched risk, a history forecaster, a fixed margin and a calibrated direct language-model forecaster that sees the same text?
claim_scope: control/calibration mechanism on the release event only. The statements are agent-authored (ineligible); results cannot be cited as evidence about human phrasing or language generalization. Source profiles are designed, not measured (docs/reproduce/maintenance_data_survey_20260925.md: no public announced-vs-measured data found).

window.start: 2026-09-30 (amendment 1: immediately after the regenerated receipt; originally 2026-10-09)
window.freeze_deadline: superseded by amendment 1: the regenerated receipt precedes the formal run
window.rule: no change of task, metric, arms, alpha, n_min, calibration window, source profiles, sequence seeds, decision rules or budgets inside the window; a bug fix is recorded in the record and forces a full rerun of every arm

task.event: release of the protected meeting (events['ended'] from the true release interval tau)
task.episode: 12 native intervals, base ledger of contracts/frozen_protocol_20260924_20261008.json, ledger v2, obligation planner, admission 'forecast', per-interval recovery-window invariant (src/vera/recovery_shield.py) for every arm unless stated
task.messages: tick 2: a release-time statement; tick 4: its backup-delay request, as in the 19 distinct statements of data/open_requests/agent_test_corpus_v4_20260923.json and chain_corpus_20260924.json selected by scripts/run_release_diagnostic.py items()

sources.residual: delta = tau - e_ref, e_ref = annotated earliest tick of the statement; tau = clip(e_ref + delta, 3, 12); tau 12 means no release inside the episode

profiles.drifting: episodes 1-15 as accurate, episodes 16-30 as early_biased

sources.sequences: 4 profiles x 5 seeds (0-4) = 20 sequences of 30 episodes; statement of each episode drawn with replacement from the 19 by the sequence seed; the same 600 (statement, tau) worlds are used by every arm
sources.secondary_profile: optional, only if the user approves prospective status-page collection and its terms of use are checked before the freeze deadline: an end-time residual profile derived from collected completion deviations, frozen with a SHA receipt before the window; otherwise omitted; never added inside the window

calibration.target: lower bound for tau with miscoverage alpha per in-episode event
calibration.memory: last 20 residuals of the same sequence
calibration.residual: r = tau - e_hat, e_hat = the estimate the arm itself used for that episode (compiled contract value, or the forecaster's answer); observed after the episode ends; tau = 12 is right-censored and recorded as 12 - e_hat (conservative for a lower quantile)
calibration.bound: k = floor(alpha * (n + 1)); if n < n_min or k = 0 the belief is 'may happen now' (A0); else e = e_hat + r_(k), the k-th smallest residual (may move the belief earlier or later)
calibration.cold_start: the first n_min episodes of every sequence run as A0 for calibrated arms and are reported separately; decisions use episodes 10-30 (evaluation episodes)

arms.A0_now: belief: the event may happen now
arms.A1_margin: belief: 6 intervals after the latest administrator message
arms.A2_history: belief: conditional 10% lower quantile of past tau in the same sequence given no release yet; A0 until 9 past tau
arms.A2p_cal_qwen7b: 7B asked directly for an earliest release interval from the past tau of the sequence and the administrator messages (release_forecast.TextForecastBelief prompt); its answers calibrated by the same algorithm
arms.A4_oracle: belief: true tau (extra information, reference only)
arms.A3_cal_annotated_legacy: calibrated annotated belief with the old one-shot timed admission and no per-interval invariant (controller-layer comparison)

metrics.primary: administrator_obligation_satisfaction per episode (frozen protocol definition, deadline at state tick D)
metrics.risk: episode recovery violation indicator over episodes whose release falls inside the episode; recovery violation intervals reported alongside
metrics.gates: deadline misses and hard-SLA violation intervals of an arm not above A0_now

analysis.uncertainty: cluster bootstrap over sequences stratified by profile, 10000 resamples, seed 0, 95% percentile intervals
analysis.risk_budget: an arm is within budget when its episode violation rate is <= 0.10 and the upper bound of its interval is <= 0.15
analysis.H1_calibration_reduces_risk: A3_cal_annotated minus A3_raw_annotated violation rate: upper bound < 0
analysis.H2_value_at_matched_risk: A3_cal_annotated within budget and passes the gates; satisfaction minus A2_history lower bound > 0 and minus A0_now lower bound > 0; for A1_margin and A2p_cal_qwen7b each: either the comparator is outside budget or A3_cal_annotated minus it has satisfaction lower bound > 0
analysis.advance: H1 and H2 hold: calibration of structured statements is a supported mechanism on this task (diagnostic scope)
analysis.narrow: if A2p_cal_qwen7b is within budget and A3_cal_annotated minus A2p_cal_qwen7b satisfaction interval covers 0 or is negative: the structured statement route has no advantage over calibrated direct forecasting; the claim is narrowed to calibrated text forecasts
analysis.stop: if A3_cal_annotated is outside budget overall or in 2 or more of the 4 profiles, or H2 fails against A2_history: calibration is not a contribution on this task; write up and stop; no re-prompting, new arms or new profiles in the window
analysis.secondary: A3_cal_qwen7b vs A3_cal_rule at matched risk (language-model attribution; parity with A3_cal_annotated means compilation is solved); A3_cal_annotated_legacy vs A3_cal_annotated (controller layer); per-profile results; cold-start episodes
analysis.not_a_failure: parity of a small or rule compiler with 7B is not evidence against language value

budgets.note_episodes: 10 arms x 600 = 6000 planned, retries included in the cap
budgets.note_calls: A2p about 1200 (history changes every episode, no cache); A3_cal_qwen7b compile results may be cached by identical prompt because decoding is greedy; the cache is declared in the report
budgets.pre_window_smoke: stand-in native only, plus at most 2 real episodes per arm for timing
budgets.numeric: 850/1000 ms and 6/2/5/2/8 operational limits unchanged; forecaster calls happen outside the numerical proposal budget
